doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Advice to young musicians about experience and money
summary: Young players lack experience and style; Levy warns them to watch lawyers and accountants and sign their own checks.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Yeah. If you were able to tell some future jazz star a couple words about what they should know about their own business. Do you have any thoughts on that?

Well, today I would tell any youngsters starting out, the most important thing is to try to get some experience with older players or people who’ve been out there. Because what’s happening now is a lot of youngsters are coming into the business and they make the records and the records sold, and they’re hot records. But they don’t have any experience about playing with anybody, you know they don’t have the experience. And they don’t really have a style. For example, when I came along, you could recognize the person by the style, how they played, the style. Today these kids, you hear them and I don’t know one from the other. I listen to them and I say who is this and who is this? They don’t have any set style, because they haven’t learned the experience. They can play, and they play with feeling and they can read better than a lot of musicians that came along during my time, but they don’t have any experience of playing with anybody. So they don’t get themselves any style and are able to listen to what these people before them. I guess Wynton and his brother and a few others that came along, they’d listen because of their parents saying, “look, this is where the roots are of this whole thing, so you’ve got to learn this first before you get to where you are when you get to Coltrane and Miles and all those people” — there’s a lot of folks came before that.
I suppose it would depend on what their parents were listening to.

That’s right. It has a lot to do with that, it has a lot to do with that. And as far as the business is concerned, I would tell them most of all please watch your lawyers and your accountant, because they’re ripping these kids off something awful, you know, it’s terrible. And take care of, make sure your own money is, don’t listen to anybody else. Sign your own checks. Make sure that you take care of your own, that end of the business. Unless you have someone very close to you who you can really trust. Because
they’ll rip you off. And the way it’s going down now they get ripped off very easily. Guys make a lot of money real fast now and it’s gone real quick.
